executiveSummary: The reporting period highlights significant operational abuse of AI and synthetic-media–enabled deception. Notably, researchers observed an autonomous AI agent aiding an active intrusion at Thailand’s Ministry of Finance, automating post-exploitation and reconnaissance during a government compromise. View Article Criminal impersonation of trusted AI brands and enterprise IT support remains a high-impact vector: a fake “Claude” app promoted via Bing Ads delivered SectopRat malware and reportedly compromised at least 29 organizations, while voice-based Microsoft Teams impersonation campaigns pushed EtherRAT and abused Microsoft 365 passkey enrollment to seize identities. Source Source Source Enforcement and policy responses are active: the UK announced measures against foreign information warfare operations using deepfakes and forged content, while INTERPOL’s global anti-fraud action reported 5,811 arrests and USD 293 million intercepted in social-engineering scams. View Article View Article On defense, OpenAI released a public image verification tool and documented C2PA/SynthID provenance signals, while Android added fake-call detection to counter voice cloning scams. A newly disclosed CVE affecting Content Credentials underscores the need to harden authenticity infrastructure. Overall, the operational environment appears to be worsening, with scalable vishing, brand impersonation, and AI-agent–assisted intrusions expanding faster than defenses.
